judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 6 Indicators (same statement-type grain, identical coordinate rank 2, no developmental gap). B6.2.3.1.2 (Strand 2 Algebra, Sub-Strand Variables and Equations, under B6.2.3.1 on single-variable one-step equations) requires identifying the unknown, representing a problem with an equation, and solving it concretely, pictorially or symbolically; B6.1.2.5.1 (Strand 1 Number, Sub-Strand Number Operations, under B6.1.2.5 'Translate word problems into mathematical sentences and solve') requires solving multi-step word problems involving the four basic operations. There is genuine conceptual coherence: both translate word-problem situations into mathematical sentences/equations and solve them, and the algebraic equation-representation work complements number-operation multi-step problem solving. However, the evidence shows no substantive same-rank dependency — the algebra indicator is scoped to one-step single-variable equations while the number indicator is scoped to multi-step four-operation computation, so neither can be shown to be the proficiency base for the other; token/trigram and code-prefix overlap are weak ('solve', 'the', shared 'b6' segment) and the shared Grade ancestor alone is not semantic evidence. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted evidence items each), so scope detail beyond the bounded excerpts is unverified.

B5.2.1.1.1 (second) has learners extend a given pattern with and without concrete materials and explain how each element differs from the preceding one — concrete, element-by-element reasoning about pattern change (LCs: 'Extend a given pattern with and without concrete materials'; 'Explain how each element of a pattern differs from the preceding one'). B5.2.1.1.8 (first) requires describing the relationship in a given table or chart using a mathematical expression, i.e. generalising the same element-to-element change into symbolic form on a tabular representation. Proficiency in concretely extending and verbalising the difference between successive elements supports success in expressing that relationship as a mathematical expression, so the direction is second_to_first. Same-rank direction rests on this substantive abstraction increase, not on indicator code order or shared parent alone; token/trigram overlap was only generic stopwords and is not treated as evidence. They sit in different Sub-Strands (Counting, Representation & Cardinality under Content Standard B5.1.1.1 place value vs Number: Fractions under B5.1.3.1 comparing/adding/subtracting/multiplying fractions), so the coherence is the shared comparison-and-ordering reasoning applied to different number types rather than a demonstrated dependency: fraction comparison relies on equivalence/common-denominator strategies not evidenced in the whole-number indicator. With equal grade rank and no substantive same-rank sequencing evidence in the supplied text, codes, or LCs (code prefix and local rank alone are not semantic), symmetric conceptual coherence is the supported judgment. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (same rank 0, same statement-type grain) but sit in different strands: B4.1.1.3.5 'Generate and analyse patterns in square numbers' under Number / Counting, Representation & Cardinality (Content Standard B4.1.1.3 on factors, multiples and squared numbers), and B4.3.3.2.4 'Develop and apply a formula for determining area of a rectangle and square' under Geometry and Measurement / Perimeter and Area (Content Standard B4.3.3.2). The shared token 'square' is used in different senses (square number vs square shape), yet the pair carries genuine, pair-specific coherence: the area formula for a square is side multiplied by itself, i.e. a squared number, and square-number patterns are standardly represented as square arrays/areas. LCs ('generate/analyse patterns in square numbers' vs 'develop/apply a formula for determining the area of a rectangle and square') show complementary numeric and measurement treatments of squaring rather than one extending or depending on the other. judgment.rationale: Same-grain Indicator pair in Strand 3 (Geometry and Measurement) whose statements are verbatim identical ('Tell the position and motion of objects in space using the cardinal points north, south, east and west') and which decompose into the same two Learning Components (telling position; telling motion using cardinal points), with jaccard 1.0 on SFI text, LC text, LC tags and shared-LC evidence. The first SFI is the BASIC 5 occurrence (rank 1, code B5.3.4.1.1, under Sub-Strand 3 Geometric Reasoning) and the second is the BASIC 4 occurrence (rank 0, code B4.3.2.1.1, under Sub-strand 2 Position / Transformation). The bounded evidence shows no change in skill demand, representation, scope or complexity between the two occurrences, so no developmental dependency is justified; the differing grade coordinate and Sub-Strand organizer label are placement/context and cannot by themselves license buildsTowards. What remains is substantive, pair-specific instructional coherence: the identical cardinal-points position-and-motion skill recurs and is reinforced across grade scopes within the same strand, which supports symmetric relatesTo. Limitations retained: both endpoints and several ancestors carry merge/code audit context (documented duplicated/misnumbered BASIC 4 Position/Transformation section; BASIC 5 items deliberately kept separate by grade scope) and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 and 40 omitted source-evidence items), so confidence is held moderate.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements in Strand 3 (Geometry and Measurement) with identical statement text: 'Tell the position and motion of objects in space using the cardinal points north, south, east and west', decomposed into the same two Learning Components (position; motion). The second SFI is the BASIC 4 occurrence (rank 0, code B4.3.2.1.1, under Sub-strand 2 Position/Transformation) and the first is the BASIC 5 occurrence (rank 1, code B5.3.4.1.1, under Sub-Strand 3 Geometric Reasoning), so the only permitted developmental direction is lower-to-higher (second_to_first). judgment.rationale: Both are Indicator-grain statements in Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement, Measurement sub-strands concerning perimeter with centimetre/metre units. The BASIC 4 indicator (rank 0, B4.3.3.1.1, under 'Demonstrate understanding of perimeter of regular and irregular shapes') has learners estimate perimeter using centimetre/metre referents, establishing unit sense and an informal grasp of perimeter. The BASIC 5 indicator (rank 1, B5.3.2.1.2, under 'Estimate and measure perimeter and surface area of 2-D shapes using centimetre and metre') requires calculating perimeter of given shapes in centimetres and metres — a substantive advance from estimation with referents to quantitative computation in the same units. Direction is lower-to-higher rank, so second_to_first buildsTowards is supported. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/code-collision audit context, but the trustworthy statement text, Strand/Sub-Strand context and Learning Components are sufficient and consistent.
